summary.text: A 57-year-old man, a farmer with no history of HIV infection, immunodeficiency or immunosuppressive drug consumption, was admitted to hospital in Isfahan with a 4-month history of a left foot cutaneous wound acquired during agriculture, persistent fever of 39 °C, weakness, persistent non-productive cough and chest pain.

Chest x-ray showed nodular lesions across both lungs, the PPD test was negative and the erythrocyte sedimentation rate was 57. Tuberculosis was suspected, Staphylococcus aureus was isolated from the foot wound and anti-tuberculosis drugs were initiated. After 2 weeks the wound had not improved and developed into a large productive lesion expelling pus similar to mycetoma.

A wound biopsy and BAL sample were cultured; PCR for Mycobacterium tuberculosis on BAL was negative. The micro-organism was identified as N. mexicana and was isolated from both BAL and the wound; direct PCR of the BAL sample and sequence analysis of the bacterial isolate from the foot wound belonged to N. mexicana. The tested isolate was susceptible to ciprofloxacin, clarithromycin, ceftriaxone and linezolid and resistant to TMP/SMX and minocycline. Disseminated infection was supposed; brain CT was normal and blood culture was negative.
The patient was initiated on linezolid and amikacin for 6 months. Respiratory symptoms recovered after 3 weeks and the foot wound gradually improved after a few weeks.

article_limitations: Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; the five JPEGs were inspected in the separate visual submission.
Isolate-level laboratory results (phenotype, biochemistry, susceptibility, 16S rRNA) are not tied by the source to BAL versus wound.

The statement that the patient was not treated after 2 weeks is unclear and no treatment failure is inferred.
No dates, hospital course dates, discharge or follow-up beyond 6 months of therapy are reported; relative timing only.
The abstract and results use plural wording although one patient is described; roster kept at one.
Discussion statements about literature cases, animals and general nocardiosis are not index-patient facts.
